analogs.covers: Herd defence: the defensive wall and harem bulls
Fighting style: a sharp-horned antelope that charges predators in hit-and-run attacks, led by a dominant bull

headline: The 'attack dog' of the ceratopsian herd: a musk-ox wall with oryx-style hit-and-run chargers.

setting.label: Nomad of dense forests and arid grasslands
setting.note: Roams dense forests or arid grasslands in huge herds. Cools off in shallow water and mud, and marks trees by sharpening its horns on them.

playsLike: You are a medium ceratopsian in an unlimited herd made of harems, led by the stag with the largest harem. You are aggressive to any species outside your ceratopsian herd. You mock-charge predators twice and then attack if they don't back off. The herd forms a defensive formation while up to 4 defenders, usually stags, charge around outside with hit-and-run attacks and chase predators out of sight. You flee pairs of Apex carnivores and grow nervous around Daspletosaurus.

why.text: Unlimited defensive formation with the young and injured behind it, the musk ox tactic (official inspiration).
Up to 4 'active' defenders charge in, land a blow and dart away, the way oryx fend off lions with their horns.
'Often referred to as attack dogs' of the mixed ceratopsian herd. It is the most aggressive ceratopsian in the group.
Each stag has a harem and the stag with the most does leads. Gemsbok herds are also led by a dominant bull.
Sharpens and scratches its horns on rocks and trees, leaving marks as high as it can reach.

notLike: Musk oxen rarely chase far; Styracosaurus defenders chase forfeiting predators until they leave the herd's line of sight.
twist: The profile even lists an 'Albino Oryx' skin.
